citation.authors: Braat S, Fielding KL, Han J et al

cited_by.title: Low haemoglobin, low or high white cells: causes, thresholds and pregnancy

record.population: Healthy reference samples from 8 data sources (USA, England, Australia, China, the Netherlands, Canada, Ecuador, Bangladesh): 3,640 non-pregnant women, 2,377 men, 772 first-trimester and 111 second-trimester pregnancies, plus children and adolescents
record.design: Pooled analysis of fifth-centile haemoglobin, with a summary of three genetic studies
record.finding: Fifth-centile haemoglobin in adults aged 18 to 65 was 119.7 g/L in non-pregnant women and 134.9 g/L in men; in pregnancy it was 110.3 g/L in the first trimester and 105.9 g/L in the second, with too little data for the third. The authors found no evidence that thresholds should differ between people of different ancestries.
record.note: These are statistical thresholds from healthy reference samples, not outcomes. Funded by WHO and the Gates Foundation.
